title: Tiered KV rendezvous fusion notes
content:
Purpose:
Short design notes and experimental results for a kernel-level rendezvous/coalescer that enables stronger fusion of attention + KV-management ops across microbatches, combined with a lightweight tiered KV cache policy. Goal is to reduce per-token cost and kernel-launch overhead for mixed workloads (many small requests + occasional long context) while keeping 99th-percentile latency targets for interactive queries.

High-level idea summary:
- Rendezvous coalescer: a tiny in-process layer that groups incoming generation requests on a single GPU into short windows (configurable 0.5–3 ms) and emits a single fused kernel invocation when possible. Instead of naive batching we form a "rendezvous group" only when all members are compatible for a fused attention+KV servicing path (similar dtypes, model variant, compatible max-seq alignment).
- Tiered KV cache: three logical tiers for KV shards: L0 = GPU DRAM (hot), L1 = host pinned memory (warm), L2 = NVMe-backed (cold). KV fetch/prefetch policies decide where to place newly-written KV entries and which keys to evict. We optimize for short-lived hot prefixes and long-running sessions with large contexts.
- Kernel fusion patterns enabled: FlashAttention-based fused attn + softmax + scaled qk + layer-norm remnants; fused qkv projection + rotary applied; merge of KV read + KV-append into the attn kernel when entries are resident or streamed from L1.

Why this is different / motivation:
- Existing microbatching and continuous-batching helps throughput but often pays heavy overhead in kernel-launch frequency for many small queries (PL). Rendezvous coalescer aims to reduce launch count without blindly increasing queue latency by making per-request latency tolerance explicit and only coalescing compatible requests.
- Paged/KV approaches today mostly treat host memory as fallback; we propose actively using host pinned memory as a warm tier with prefetch hints and a cheap async migration path to GPU when access patterns show repeat hits.

Rendezvous coalescer: design notes
- API contract: each request carries metadata: model-id, variant-hash, max_output_tokens, allowed_latency_slop_ms (optional). The coalescer respects allowed_latency_slop_ms; latency-sensitive requests (slop = 0) are never delayed.
- Grouping constraints: all requests in a rendezvous must target same compiled kernel signature (same head count/hidden-size pad to tile), similar prefix length distribution (within X tokens) to avoid pathological padding overhead, and must not require incompatible tooling (function-calls vs streaming-only).
- Windowing strategy: dynamic window based on in-flight load and target p99 SLO. When load low, window = 3 ms to maximize fusion. When load high and queue latency rises above threshold, window shrinks to 0.5 ms.
- Rendezvous buffer: small preallocated buffer of request descriptors + per-request KV pointers. The buffer drives a single kernel launch that iterates over the group members with per-member lane masks. Kernel uses warp-level predicates to skip inactive lanes.
- Fault isolation: if one request fails (bad input or OOM), we return an error for that request only and continue for others. Implementation uses a cancellation flag per-lane.

Kernel-level fusion primitives
- Use FlashAttention core for attn compute but extend head loop to accept multi-prefix mask and per-lane sequence lengths. This reuses the blockwise softmax and avoids separate per-request launches.
- KV read fusion: when KV for a group member is present in L0, kernel reads directly. When KV in L1, we start an async host->device memcpy overlapped with per-request precompute and scheduling (requires careful stream ordering). If KV cold (L2), decision point: either stall rendezvous until async NVMe->host fetch completes (higher latency) or skip fusion and service that request with fallback path.
- Append semantics: new KV writes from generation are appended into the tiered cache. For rendezvous, we emit a compacted delta of appended KV to avoid multiple small writes; a single coalesced NVMe write/host memcpy for the group when suitable.

Tiered KV policy details
- Slot layout: KV shards split into fixed-size slabs (e.g., 128-token slabs per session). Each slab maintains metadata: last-access-epoch, hit-count, resident-tier (L0/L1/L2).
- Eviction: epoch-based aging + frequency decay. On memory pressure, evict slabs with low freq and old epoch to L1; if L1 full, start background async flush to NVMe and mark resident-tier=L2.
- Promotion: when slab hit-count crosses threshold within a short epoch window, schedule async transfer to L0. Promotion is rate-limited to avoid thrashing.
- Coalesced prefetch hint: runtime can predict next slab access by analyzing sequence length of request; prefetch for a rendezvous group if group has >M% probability of accessing slab S based on recent sessions.

Scheduling interactions and integration
- SLO-aware router: routing layer tags requests with latency slop. Scheduler uses these tags to decide whether to route to rendezvous-capable GPU nodes (favor cheaper instances) or strict-low-latency nodes (no coalescing).
- Autoscaler signals: rendezvous groups can yield higher throughput but also increase bursty memory pressure (many Ks read/writes). Autoscaler must consider settled resident-tier metrics when scaling out.

Microbenchmarks (toy numbers, local experiments)
- Setup: A100-80GB node, model variant trimmed to 12B, configure rendezvous window=2ms, group pad to 8 token blocks.
- Workload: 70% short requests (prompt+max_out=32), 30% long-session appends (context growth to 8k).
- Results: average tokens/sec improved 1.45x vs naive per-request launch; 95th p99 latency for short queries increased by 0.8ms (median +0.1ms) when allowed slop=2ms. Cold-cache NVMe-heavy spots still dominated p99; rendezvous avoids cold reads by preferring groups with resident L0 or L1.
- Kernel launch count: dropped from ~1200 launches/s to ~430 launches/s under the same throughput target.

Open questions / experiments to run
- Optimal slab size: evaluate 64/128/256-token slab sizes for eviction/promotion tradeoffs.
- Rendezvous fairness: measure starvation risk for long-tail low-traffic sessions and design a priority aging counter.
- Host->GPU pinned memory throughput sensitivity: measure impact across instance types and PCIe vs NVLink.
- Failure modes when NVMe IO is sporadic: implement graceful degradation to fallback per-request path if NVMe latency spikes exceed threshold.

Implementation plan + milestones
- Spike (2 weeks): implement coalescer shim that groups on same model-id and measures launch reduction (no fusion changes yet).
- Kernel prototype (3–4 weeks): adapt FlashAttention kernel to accept multi-prefix masks and run small microbenchmarks.
- Tiered KV shim (3 weeks): implement slab metadata, async host pinned copy + simple eviction policy.
- Integration & experiments (2–3 weeks): combine coalescer + kernel + tiered KV and run production-like workload in staging.

Notes / references
- See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3412 (initial rendezvous coalescer shim)
- Related discussion: slack thread C03ENGXYZ (rendezvous heuristics)
- Jira: JIRA-RT-1284 tracks design -> prototype -> rollout tasks.

Unresolved design decisions (short list)
- Should rendezvous be enabled by default per-customer or opt-in on per-route basis? (prefer opt-in for now until p99s are proven)
- What telemetry to expose in console: per-route coalescing ratio, resident-tier hit rates, average extra latency introduced by coalescing.

Summary:
Rendezvous fusion + tiered KV provides a concrete path to reduce kernel-launch overheads and token-level unit cost for mixed workloads. The approach trades small, bounded extra latency (configurable per-request) for a meaningful reduction in kernel launches and better amortization of attention kernels. Next steps: run the proposed spike, collect telemetry, iterate on slab sizing and coalescing window heuristics.

Notes to self:
- Keep the first deploy gated behind feature-flag per-route.
- Add unit tests for lane cancellation semantics and single-request fallbacks.
- Add simple dashboard panel for "coalesce ratio" and "tier hit rate" before wider rollout.
